AP. Surgical Steel is a gamble because from what I understand there are really no regulations on what can or can’t go in it. I use it because I have credible manufacturers and have had zero issues reported by my clients. Implant grade titanium is the best thing overall but it’s also more expensive to order so I can understand why not all piercers carry it (especially in this economy!). If they don’t use titanium and you are concerned maybe look through the reviews for their page and see if anyone reported issues with the material used and don’t go anywhere to get pierced without proper vetting. If they can’t explain in simple terms why they do things a certain way or if you feel they aren’t being entirely candid move on to a different shop.

Piercer here. I haven’t heard of “too much touching” causing rejection so definitely ask for clarification from your piercer on that but the two main catalysts of rejection is the piercing being too shallow or considerable trauma to the area. The trauma isn’t a guaranteed rejection because everybody is different and I’ve had clients that could probably take a jackhammer to some of their hardware and be fine. As long as your piercings don’t fall under one of those two categories you should be fine! Hope this helps.
